item.title: China to implement mortgage interest subsidies to unlock housing demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
China to implement mortgage interest subsidies to unlock housing demand BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- China will implement interest subsidies for housing loans starting Oct. 1, 2026, as part of efforts to help reduce home-buying costs and better unlock the housing demand of residents. With a tentative implementation period of one year, the fiscal authorities will provide an annualized subsidy of 1 percentage point for eligible first-time homebuyers, according to a notice jointly issued by the Ministry of Finance, the People's Bank of China and the National Financial Regulatory Administration on Tuesday. This is the first time the central government has offered interest subsidies on commercial housing loans. This interest subsidy policy is focused on first-time homebuyers. The floor area of each purchased unit must not exceed 120 square meters, and the purchase price must not surpass 1.5 million yuan (about 222,516 U.S. dollars). Under this policy, the maximum amount of interest-subsidized loans can reach 1 million yuan, and the subsidy period can extend up to five years. According to estimates, for a long-term 1-million-yuan commercial personal mortgage, the subsidies could help borrowers reduce cumulative interest payments by nearly 50,000 yuan. By defining housing price, floor area and loan category, the policy aims to precisely benefit target groups and help lower-income families reduce their monthly mortgage burdens, the departments said. The policy focuses on first-time buyers with essential needs, supporting families in purchasing small and medium-sized, and relatively low-priced homes, according to the departments. The policy is expected to reduce the mortgage burden for new urban residents, newly employed college graduates, and urban wage-earning families, said Luo Zhiheng, chief economist at Yuekai Securities. In recent years, China has introduced supply-side measures to support the development of the real estate market, including supporting the issuance of new special-purpose bonds for land reserves and supporting local governments in purchasing existing commercial housing for use as affordable housing. This time, the focus has shifted to the demand side, further expanding policy efforts through fiscal-financial coordination. Industry insiders believe that interest subsidies can reduce home-buying costs, accelerate the destocking of new homes, and ease the funding pressure on real estate developers. The policy clearly demonstrates strong support for rigid home-buying demand, or first-home demand, and will in turn influence subsequent replacement and upgrading demand, said Yan Yuejin, deputy director at E-house China R&D Institute. Li Yujia, chief researcher at the Guangdong Housing Policy Research Center, said the interest subsidy policy will reduce the cost of residents' mortgage loans and improve their willingness to take on leverage, thereby restoring the financial accelerator effect of the real estate sector. Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics earlier this month showed narrower year-on-year declines in home prices across major Chinese cities in August, pointing to further signs of stabilization. In August, Chinese authorities deepened reforms to the housing provident fund system, and refined regulations on commercial housing sales and property financing. The package of policies is working in a coordinated manner from both the supply and demand sides, aiming to improve market expectations, restore residents' willingness to buy homes, and promote the steady and healthy development of the real estate market, experts said. item.title: China outlines sci-tech priorities for 2026-2030 to underpin high-quality development
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
China outlines sci-tech priorities for 2026-2030 to underpin high-quality development BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- China will strengthen basic research, tackle core technologies and speed up the industrial application of research results during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) to better support high-quality development, officials of the Ministry of Science and Technology said on Tuesday. At a press conference held by the State Council Information Office, Minister of Science and Technology Yin Hejun said China's total R&D spending exceeded 3.92 trillion yuan (about 582 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, or 2.8 percent of GDP. This amount exceeded the average among the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) members for the first time. China has ranked first in the world for many consecutive years in international patent applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) and in papers published in high-level international journals, Yin said. China ranks ninth among 60 countries in overall national innovation capability, according to the National Innovation Index Report 2025 released by the Chinese Academy of Science and Technology for Development. Looking ahead, basic research will be organized in areas such as mathematical theory and applications, control of states of matter, synthetic biology, the materials genome, controlled nuclear fusion and intelligent scientist systems, Yin said. He also called for faster application of artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific research to lead a shift in how research is carried out. Paramount core technologies are another important priority, Yin said. China will push for progress along the entire innovation chain in key fields such as integrated circuits, machine tools and high-end instruments, and step up R&D in frontier technologies including AI, quantum technology, biotechnology and brain-computer interfaces. Sci-tech innovation should also deliver more quality products and services that improve people's well-being, he said, with tasks laid out in areas including environmental pollution control, resource recycling, agricultural biological breeding, innovative drug development, high-end medical equipment and responses to population aging. On turning research results into real-world productivity, Zhang Guangjun, vice minister of science and technology, said China will break the stereotype of producing results first and considering their application later on. Policies will instead direct research to where demand lies and ensure that results, once achieved, can be put to use, so that scientific and industrial innovation are planned in tandem and support one another, he said. Zhang also called for stronger enterprise-led collaboration among industry, universities and research institutes, with innovation resources such as projects, platforms, data, talent and funding channeled to enterprises. Proof-of-concept and pilot-scale testing platforms will be built to help technologies mature and upgrade faster, he said. Venture capital has played a vital role, with investors increasingly backing early-stage and small companies, taking a long-term view and focusing on hard technology, said Qiu Yong, vice minister of science and technology. New funds raised in the equity investment market exceeded 1 trillion yuan in the first half of 2026, up 49 percent year on year, he said, citing statistics from relevant institutions. Universities are adjusting their disciplines to meet urgent national needs, he said. China will continue to build Beijing and the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, Shanghai and the wider Yangtze River Delta, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area into international sci-tech innovation centers, Yin said. The three centers account for 58.8 percent of the country's R&D spending and 81.1 percent of its PCT international patent applications, and are helping drive innovation in surrounding provinces and municipalities and across the country. R&D spending in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region has reached 4.48 percent of regional GDP, with major sci-tech achievements emerging in fields such as AI and biomanufacturing, Yin said. The Yangtze River Delta accounts for nearly 30 percent of the country's basic research spending, with corporate spending on basic research up 38.3 percent year on year in 2025. It has witnessed key breakthroughs in areas such as integrated circuits and quantum technology, he said. The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area draws on Guangdong's industrial innovation strengths and the science and education resources of Hong Kong and Macao, Yin said. Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao have jointly built 35 laboratories, and produced 14,000 papers under international collaboration. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China's manufacturing PMI at 50.1 in September
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
China's manufacturing PMI at 50.1 in September BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- The purchasing managers' index (PMI) for China's manufacturing sector stood at 50.1 in September 2026, up 0.3 percentage points from August and back to the expansion zone, official data showed on Wednesday. A reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signifies contraction. The manufacturing sector's business climate improved further in September, with the PMI rising for a second consecutive month, said Huo Lihui, a chief statistician with the National Bureau of Statistics. Among the 21 industries surveyed, 12 reported a PMI above the expansion threshold, four more than the previous month, Huo noted. The sector saw expansion in both manufacturing output and market demand in September. The production sub-index climbed to 51.7, up 1.3 percentage points from August, while the new orders index was at 50.5, still above the threshold. Driven by the acceleration in production, enterprises' willingness to purchase strengthened, with the procurement volume index reaching 51.0, an increase of 0.5 percentage points from the previous month, said Huo. PMI for the equipment manufacturing industry, the high-tech manufacturing industry and the consumer goods industry stood at 51, 52.5 and 50.7, respectively, all remaining in the expansion zone. Affected by rising international commodity prices and growing demand in some industries, the purchasing price index for major raw materials and the ex-factory price index for manufacturing stood at 60.8 and 54, respectively, up 4.2 percentage points and 3.6 percentage points from the previous month. PMI for medium-sized and small manufacturing enterprises came in at 49.7 and 48.9, respectively, increases of 0.3 percentage points and 1 percentage point from the previous month, as business activity picked up. Xi's article on people's wellbeing to be published (Xinhua) 16:03, September 30, 2026
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- An article by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on improving the people's wellbeing will be published on Thursday. The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 19th issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. The article is a collection of excerpts of Xi's important discourses on the issue between November 2012 and January 2026. (Web editor: Zhang Kaiwei, Liang Jun)

item.title: Xi, Brunei's Sultan exchange congratulations on 35th anniversary of ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Xi, Brunei's Sultan exchange congratulations on 35th anniversary of ties BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Sultan of Brunei Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mu'izzaddin Waddaulah on Wednesday exchanged congratulations on the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Xi noted that the traditional friendship between China and Brunei has a long history and remained strong over time. In the process of working together towards modernization, the two countries have set an example of mutual respect, equality and common development between large and small countries, Xi added. Over the 35 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China and Brunei have steadily deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful results in cooperation across various fields, and strengthened people-to-people exchanges, he said. Xi said that last year, Hassanal paid a state visit to China, during which the two sides reached important consensus on building a China-Brunei community with a shared future, ushering bilateral relations into a new stage of historical development. Xi emphasized that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Brunei relations and is willing to work with Hassanal to take the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties as an opportunity to carry forward traditional friendship, enhance the alignment of development strategies, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and advance the building of the China-Brunei community with a shared future in a more substantive and in-depth manner, so as to better benefit the two peoples and contribute more to regional prosperity and stability. Hassanal stated that over the past 35 years since establishing diplomatic relations, Brunei and China have consistently trusted, respected, and understood each other. In 2025, the two countries reached an important consensus on building a community with a shared future, he added. He looks forward to taking the 35th anniversary of Brunei-China diplomatic relations as an opportunity to further strengthen bilateral ties, deepen cooperation and exchanges in areas such as economy, trade, investment, defense, and culture, and jointly achieve prosperity and progress for both countries, thereby better benefiting their peoples. Tourism booms along Pinglu Canal in S China's Guangxi An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 29, 2026 shows cruise boats at a waterway service area of Pinglu Canal in Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Tourism is booming along the Pinglu Canal in Guangxi recently. Many tourists take boat tours to view waterways, navigation hubs and bridges of the canal and enjoy the scenery along it.
